bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; increasing criminal penalties and expanding the scope of the doxxing crime; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 609.5151.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 609.5151, is amended to read:

609.5151 DISSEMINATION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION [-ABOUT LAW ENFORCEMENT-] PROHIBITED; PENALTY.

Subdivision 1.
Definitions.
As used in this section:
(1) "family or household member" has the meaning given in section 518B.01, subdivision 2;
(2) "law enforcement official" means both peace officers as defined in section 626.84, subdivision 1, and persons employed by a law enforcement agency; and
(3) "personal information" means a home telephone number, personal cell number, personal email address, name of the [-official's-][+ person's+] minor child, photographs of the [-official's-][+ person's+] minor child, home address, directions to a home, or photographs of a home.

Subd. 2.
Crime described.
[-(a)-] It is a [-misdemeanor for a person-][+ crime+] to knowingly and without consent make publicly available, including but not limited to through the Internet, personal information about [-a law enforcement official or an official's-][+ another person or a+] family or household member[+ of that person+], if:
(1) the public availability of information poses an imminent and serious threat to the [-official's-][+ other person's+] safety or the safety of [-an official's-][+ that person's+] family or household member; and
(2) the person making the information publicly available knows or reasonably should know of the imminent and serious threat.

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Penalty.+]

[+(a) A violation of subdivision 2 is a misdemeanor unless the victim is a law enforcement official or a family or household member of a law enforcement official, in which case it is a gross misdemeanor. +]

(b) A [-person is guilty of a gross misdemeanor if the person violates paragraph (a) and a law enforcement official or an official's family or household member-][+ violation of subdivision 2 is a felony punishable by imprisonment for not more than two years or to the payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both, if the victim or the victim's family or household member+] suffers great bodily harm or death as a result of the violation.
(c) A person who is convicted of a second or subsequent violation of this section is guilty of a [-gross misdemeanor-][+ felony punishable by imprisonment for not more than two years or to the payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both+].

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to crimes committed on or after that date. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; increasing criminal penalties and expanding the scope of the doxxing crime; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 609.5151.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 609.5151, is amended to read:

609.5151 DISSEMINATION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION PROHIBITED; PENALTY.

Subdivision 1.
Definitions.
As used in this section:
(1) "family or household member" has the meaning given in section 518B.01, subdivision 2;
(2) "law enforcement official" means both peace officers as defined in section 626.84, subdivision 1, and persons employed by a law enforcement agency; and
(3) "personal information" means a home telephone number, personal cell number, personal email address, name of the person's minor child, photographs of the person's minor child, home address, directions to a home, or photographs of a home.

Subd. 2.
Crime described.
It is a crime to knowingly and without consent make publicly available, including but not limited to through the Internet, personal information about another person or a family or household member of that person, if:
(1) the public availability of information poses an imminent and serious threat to the other person's safety or the safety of that person's family or household member; and
(2) the person making the information publicly available knows or reasonably should know of the imminent and serious threat.

Subd. 3.

Penalty.

(a) A violation of subdivision 2 is a misdemeanor unless the victim is a law enforcement official or a family or household member of a law enforcement official, in which case it is a gross misdemeanor.

(b) A violation of subdivision 2 is a felony punishable by imprisonment for not more than two years or to the payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both, if the victim or the victim's family or household member suffers great bodily harm or death as a result of the violation.
(c) A person who is convicted of a second or subsequent violation of this section is guilty of a felony punishable by imprisonment for not more than two years or to the payment of a fine of not more than $4,000, or both.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to crimes committed on or after that date.
